subject: Telecommunication and Computer Networks
chapters: Chapter 5: Physical and Data Link Layer

questions.text: Explain the basic elements of a Telecommunication System with a neat block diagram. Discuss the transmission impairments (Attenuation, Distortion, and Noise) in guided media (Twisted pair, Coaxial cable, Optical fiber) vs unguided media.

Compare the transmission modes: Simplex, Half-Duplex, and Full-Duplex with practical telecommunication examples. What are the advantages of optical fiber over coaxial cables in backbone telecom networks?

Explain the evolution of switching systems from manual to electromechanical (Strowger, Crossbar) and electronic switching. Differentiate between Space Division Switching and Time Division Switching. Explain the working of a Time-Space-Time (TST) switch with a neat diagram.

Explain the FDM and TDM hierarchies used in telecommunications. Compare E1 (2.048 Mbps, 32 channels) and T1 (1.544 Mbps, 24 channels) carrier systems. Explain Common Channel Signaling System No. 7 (SS7) protocol architecture (MTP 1-3, SCCP, ISUP, TCAP).

Define Traffic Intensity, Erlang, CCS, and Busy Hour Traffic. In a telephone exchange, 1,200 calls are received during a busy hour with an average call holding time of 3 minutes. Calculate the traffic load in Erlangs and CCS. Differentiate between Loss Systems (Erlang-B) and Delay Systems (Erlang-C).
Explain Grade of Service (GoS) and Blocking Probability in telecommunications. Discuss the standard telephone numbering plan (E.164) and telephone charging plans (flat rate vs metered billing).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Physical and Data Link Layer
questions.text: Explain the 7-layer OSI Reference Model and compare it in detail with the 4/5-layer TCP/IP Protocol Suite. Explain the process of data encapsulation and decapsulation as data moves down and up the protocol stack.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Physical and Data Link Layer
questions.text: Explain the working principle and operating layer of the following network interconnection devices: (a) Repeater & Hub (Physical Layer), (b) Bridge & Switch (Data Link Layer), (c) Router (Network Layer), (d) Gateway (Application Layer).

Differentiate between Circuit Switching, Packet Switching (Datagram approach), and Virtual Circuit Switching. Explain digital line encoding techniques: Manchester, Differential Manchester, NRZ-I, and MLT-3 with waveform diagrams for the bit sequence .

Explain Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) error detection. A bit sequence 00100$ is to be transmitted with generator polynomial (x) = x^3 + x^2 + 1$. Find the transmitted codeword and show how the receiver detects an error if the 3rd bit is inverted.

Explain Medium Access Control (MAC) protocols: Pure ALOHA, Slotted ALOHA, CSMA/CD (Ethernet IEEE 802.3), and CSMA/CA (Wi-Fi IEEE 802.11). Derive the maximum theoretical throughput of Pure ALOHA (8.4\%$) and Slotted ALOHA (6.8\%$).

An organization is granted the block 00.10.0.0/16$. Using Variable Length Subnet Masking (VLSM), design subnets for 4 departments requiring 120, 60, 30, and 14 host addresses respectively. For each subnet, find the Subnet Mask, Network Address, Usable Host Range, and Broadcast Address.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Physical and Data Link Layer
questions.text: Compare Distance Vector Routing (RIP) vs Link State Routing (OSPF) with respect to convergence speed, routing metrics, and link-state advertisements (LSAs). Explain the Count-to-Infinity problem in RIP and its mitigation (Split Horizon and Poison Reverse).

Explain IPv4 header format with descriptions of TTL, Fragmentation Offset, and Protocol fields. Compare IPv4 vs IPv6 addressing. Explain IPv6 transition strategies: Dual Stack, Tunneling (6to4), and NAT-PT.

Explain Network Address Translation (NAT) and Port Address Translation (PAT). Differentiate between private IP address ranges (RFC 1918) and public IP addresses. Explain how Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) resolves IP to MAC address.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Physical and Data Link Layer
questions.text: Compare Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP). Draw the TCP 3-way handshake for connection establishment and 4-way handshake for connection teardown. Explain the TCP State Transition Diagram.
Explain TCP Congestion Control mechanisms: Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance, Fast Retransmit, and Fast Recovery (AIMD). Differentiate between Leaky Bucket and Token Bucket traffic shaping algorithms.

Explain the Domain Name System (DNS) hierarchy, recursive vs iterative queries, and resource records (A, AAAA, MX, CNAME, PTR). Explain the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) DORA process (Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Physical and Data Link Layer
questions.text: Explain the working of Application Layer protocols: HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 (Persistent connections, Pipelining), FTP (Control Port 21 vs Data Port 20), and Email delivery (SMTP, POP3, IMAP). Explain Voice over IP (VoIP) architecture and SIP signaling.

Explain the fundamentals of Network Security (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, Authentication, Non-Repudiation). Compare Symmetric Encryption (AES, DES) vs Asymmetric Encryption (RSA, Diffie-Hellman). Explain SSL/TLS handshake and IPsec (AH and ESP modes).

Write technical notes on: (a) Software-Defined Networking (SDN architecture: Control plane vs Data plane, OpenFlow), (b) 5G Network Fundamentals (eMBB, URLLC, mMTC, Network Slicing), (c) Internet of Things (IoT) & Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN).

Explain the fundamental theoretical concepts, governing principles, and standard analytical methods associated with Network Layer. Draw neat diagrams and derive key mathematical formulations where applicable.

Explain the fundamental theoretical concepts, governing principles, and standard analytical methods associated with Transport Layer. Draw neat diagrams and derive key mathematical formulations where applicable.

Explain the fundamental theoretical concepts, governing principles, and standard analytical methods associated with Application Layer. Draw neat diagrams and derive key mathematical formulations where applicable.

Explain the fundamental theoretical concepts, governing principles, and standard analytical methods associated with Advanced Topics. Draw neat diagrams and derive key mathematical formulations where applicable.
